findings.title: Unrelated audit log and paginator changes with broken pagination logic and crash risks
findings.body:
The changes in `src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py`, `src/sentry/api/paginator.py`, and `src/sentry/utils/cursors.py` are completely unrelated to the PR's purpose (span buffer eviction) and introduce multiple severe defects:

1. **Null dereference on `organization_context.member` (`organization_auditlogs.py:71`)**: For superusers or requests using an organization integration token who are not members of the organization, `organization_context.member` is `None`. If `request.user.is_superuser` is `False` (or for non-member tokens), evaluating `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises an `AttributeError`.
2. **Type mismatch on `datetime` field (`organization_auditlogs.py:79`, `paginator.py:839-843`)**: `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` orders by `-datetime` (a `DateTimeField`), which is why the standard path uses `DateTimePaginator`. `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` passes `getattr(item, 'datetime')` (a `datetime` instance) to `math.floor()` / `math.ceil()`, raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. Furthermore, `value_from_cursor` returns an integer cursor value directly instead of converting it to a `datetime`, causing invalid comparisons against the timestamp column in SQL.
3. **`ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported` in Django QuerySets (`paginator.py:182-184` and `paginator.py:877-886`)**: Contrary to the comments claiming Django ORM handles negative slicing, Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly raises `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")` whenever `start < 0` or `stop < 0`. Passing a cursor with a negative `offset` (e.g., `cursor=0:-10:1` or with `enable_advanced_features=True`) will crash with an unhandled 500 error.

findings.title: Evicted spans leave orphaned entries in the redirect hash and can evict the root span
findings.body:
In `src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua` (lines 62-64), when a segment's sorted set exceeds 1000 spans, `zpopmin` evicts the spans with the lowest `end_timestamp_precise`. This causes two problems when flushing in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py`:

1. **Orphaned redirects and split segments**: `add-buffer.lua` (line 40) records `hset(main_redirect_key, span_id, set_span_id)` for every incoming span before eviction. In `done_flush_segments` (lines 478-482), `hdel` only removes `span_id`s present in `flushed_segment.spans`. Any span that was evicted by `zpopmin` is no longer in the sorted set, so its redirect entry in `span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id}` is never deleted (until the 1-hour TTL expires). Worse, if `set_span_id` itself is evicted from the sorted set, `done_flush_segments` will not delete `set_span_id` from `main_redirect_key`, while future child spans will still redirect to `set_span_id`. Additionally, the root/segment span itself can be evicted if it has an earlier `end_timestamp_precise` than its children (e.g. async child spans finishing after the root span), resulting in a flushed segment with `has_root_span = False` and no root span.
2. **Inconsistent `max_segment_spans`**: `SpansBuffer.__init__` still defines `self.max_segment_spans = max_segment_spans` (default 1001, line 150/158), which is now unused because the limit is hardcoded to `1000` in `add-buffer.lua`.
